attributes.name: Tip Type
attributes.description: The recess a driver bit engages. The single most consequential field on a driver bit: a Phillips bit in a square recess destroys the fastener, and the two are visually similar enough at a glance that the listing has to be right.

attributes.name: Tip Size
attributes.description: The size designator within the tip type, recorded as written. A string because the numbering is per-family and not comparable across families: #2 Phillips and #2 Square are different sizes, and T20 Torx is not "20" of anything the others measure.

attributes.name: Overall Length
attributes.description: Overall length of a driver bit or drill bit. Reach rather than capability, but the reason a buyer holds several of the same tip: a 1" insert bit will not reach into a joist hanger.

attributes.name: Shank
attributes.description: The shank profile a bit presents to the tool. A hard compatibility fact: an SDS-Plus bit does not go in a keyed chuck and a round-shank bit will not lock into an impact driver, so a mismatch here is a returned order rather than a compromise.

attributes.name: Pack Quantity
attributes.description: Number of units in the consumer pack the part number sells as. Distinct from case_quantity, which counts packs in a shipping carton: a "3pk" of lamps is one sellable unit containing three lamps, and confusing the two misprices the line.

attributes.name: Blade Material
attributes.description: Construction of the cutting edge. Governs which workpiece the blade survives and how many times it can be resharpened, and is usually the difference between two otherwise identical blade listings.

attributes.name: Drive Size
attributes.description: The output drive a powered driver, wrench or ratchet presents. A string because the values mix square-drive fractions with hex designations — 1/2" square and 1/4" hex are different interfaces that a bare fraction could not distinguish.

attributes.name: Product Series
attributes.description: Manufacturer's series or family designation only, without the word "series" and without the manufacturer name. The anchor for part-number grammar induction, because the positional encoding of a smart part number is defined per series rather than per manufacturer.

attributes.name: Material Application
attributes.description: The materials the product is intended to be used on. Multivalued because a single wheel is commonly rated for several, and reporting only the first would understate what the buyer can do with it.

attributes.name: Color
attributes.description: Finish or colourway as the manufacturer names it. A merchandising attribute: buyers filter on it heavily, and the manufacturer's own name for a finish is what shoppers search, so it is recorded verbatim rather than mapped to a generic colour.

attributes.name: Selling Unit of Measure
attributes.description: The unit in which the product is sold, which is not necessarily the unit in which it is priced or stocked. Conflating the three is a classic source of order errors.

attributes.name: Weight (Each)
attributes.description: Shipping weight of a single unit. Distinguish carefully from carton weight; datasheets often place them in adjacent columns with similar headings.

attributes.name: Additional Information
attributes.description: Comma-separated residual specifications the class has no dedicated attribute for, in the client's own overflow convention, e.g. "240 kW-hr Annual Energy, 1 to 12 hr Delay Start Hours". A holding pen, not a dumping ground: anything appearing here repeatedly across a category is a missing attribute and should be promoted to one.
example_values: 240 kW-hr Annual Energy, 1 to 12 hr Delay Start Hours
Folding Tines, Leak Detection System, Normal Cycle

attributes.name: Warranty
attributes.description: Warranty coverage as stated by the manufacturer, including duration and what it covers, e.g. "1 Year Manufacturer, 1 Year Labor and Parts". Recorded as published: summarising it into a single duration loses the parts/labour distinction that determines what a claim actually pays for.
example_values: 1 Year Manufacturer, 1 Year Labor and Parts

attributes.name: Approvals and Listings
attributes.description: Third-party certifications, listings and approvals explicitly stated in the source. Record only what is stated. A listing number without a recognised mark is not an approval, and an approval for one size in a series does not extend to the others.

allowed_values.note: Generic NSF mark with no standard named. Deliberately not aliased onto NSF-61: a potable-water claim needs the specific standard, and treating this as equivalent would let a cross-field rule pass on evidence that does not support it.
eye and face protection impact rating
hand protection cut, abrasion and puncture rating
building-code evaluation report for a structural or envelope product
composite decking and railing performance standard

attributes.name: Country of Origin
attributes.description: Country where the product is manufactured, as stated by the manufacturer. Drives tariff treatment and trade-agreement eligibility, so a guess here has direct financial consequences.

attributes.name: GTIN / UPC
attributes.description: Global Trade Item Number, 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits. The final digit is a modulo-10 check digit, which L0 validation verifies arithmetically — a transposed digit is therefore detectable without any external lookup.

cross_field_rules.expr: bit_tip_size is null or bit_length is not null
cross_field_rules.message: A tip size was captured with no overall length. The two figures sit adjacent in every description in this cohort — '2" #2 Phillips' — and a length that went missing usually means both tokens were read into the same field.
Bit assortments are sold by the piece count and it is stated as a bare "5pc" or "5pk" beside a real length. A count below one means a dimension was captured instead.
